objects.name: CTFT Project
objects.description: Capture-The-Flag Techniques - complementary to MITRE ATT&CK, generalized from FOM.

objects.name: Web Exploitation
objects.description: Hiding/recovering flags inside web applications, APIs and client-side code. (HTB: Web)

objects.name: Binary Exploitation
objects.description: Hiding flags behind memory-corruption gates and constrained runtime puzzles. (HTB: Pwn)

objects.name: Reverse Engineering
objects.description: Concealing logic in binaries/bytecode and reconstructing it. (HTB: Reversing)

objects.name: Cryptography
objects.description: Deliberately weakened or layered crypto and its cryptanalysis. (HTB: Crypto)

objects.name: Forensics
objects.description: Disk/memory/network artifact concealment and DFIR recovery. (HTB: Forensics)

objects.name: Steganography
objects.description: Embedding data in carriers (image/audio/text) and extracting it. (HTB: Forensics/Misc (Stego))

objects.name: Hardware
objects.description: Hiding data in embedded interfaces/signals and physically extracting it. (HTB: Hardware)

objects.name: Mobile
objects.description: Secrets concealed in mobile apps and runtime, recovered statically/dynamically. (HTB: Mobile)

objects.name: OSINT
objects.description: Information dispersed across public sources and correlated back together. (HTB: OSINT)

objects.name: Blockchain
objects.description: On-chain/contract concealment and EVM-level recovery. (HTB: Blockchain)

objects.name: Cloud
objects.description: Cloud misconfiguration concealment and enumeration-based recovery. (HTB: Cloud)

objects.name: ICS / SCADA
objects.description: Industrial-protocol register/memory hiding and protocol-level extraction. (HTB: ICS)

objects.name: AI / ML
objects.description: Secrets inside models/prompts/serialized artifacts and their extraction. (HTB: AI-ML)

objects.name: CTFTTE-FOR-001 - Magic-byte / file-signature tampering
objects.description: The author corrupts or swaps the file's magic header (e.g. flips PNG 89504E47 to a bogus value) so type detection and viewers fail. | ATT&CK complementarity: Closest ATT&CK context is T1027 (Obfuscated Files), but ATT&CK omits the byte-level magic-header recovery detail that defines this CTF technique.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FOR-001 - Recover the legitimate file signature
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Compare bytes against a signature table, identify the true type from structure/footers, and patch the header with a hex editor or python. || FORENSIC (analyst): During carving, signature-based recovery reconstructs files whose extension or header was altered; corroborate with internal structure, not just the leading bytes.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FOR-002 - Slack-space and unallocated-area concealment
objects.description: Flag data is written into file slack, unallocated clusters, or between partitions where directory entries do not point. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent; this is media-forensics carving craft.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FOR-002 - Carve hidden files from slack/unallocated space
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Run file-carving over the raw image to extract artifacts independent of the filesystem index. || FORENSIC (analyst): Treat the image at the block level; carving + manual cluster inspection recovers data the filesystem no longer references.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FOR-003 - Timestomping (MACB manipulation)
objects.description: Author rewrites file timestamps so the relevant artifact blends into a noisy timeline or appears older/newer than reality. | ATT&CK complementarity: Complements T1070.006 (Timestomp) but adds the CTF-grade MFT attribute-diff recovery procedure.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FOR-003 - Detect and reconstruct true timestamps
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): On NTFS, compare $STANDARD_INFORMATION vs $FILE_NAME timestamps; mismatches reveal manipulation and often the real ordering. || FORENSIC (analyst): Cross-reference MFT, $LogFile/$UsnJrnl, registry and event logs; timestamps that disagree across sources expose the stomped value.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FOR-004 - NTFS Alternate Data Stream hiding
objects.description: Payload is stored in a named ADS (file.txt:secret) that is invisible to ordinary directory listings. | ATT&CK complementarity: Complements T1564.004 (NTFS File Attributes); CTFT adds the extraction recipe and MFT-attribute view.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FOR-004 - Enumerate and extract Alternate Data Streams
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): List streams (dir /r, Get-Item -Stream) and read the named stream directly. || FORENSIC (analyst): Enumerate $DATA attributes per MFT record; non-default named streams are immediate indicators of concealment.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FOR-005 - Memory-resident artifact concealment
objects.description: The flag exists only in RAM (process heap, clipboard, decrypted blob) and never touches disk in plaintext. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK technique; this is volatile-memory DFIR.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FOR-005 - Recover secrets from a memory image
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Profile the dump, list processes, scan for strings/patterns, and dump the owning process's address space. || FORENSIC (analyst): Volatility plugins reconstruct process lists, network state, command history and injected regions to locate transient secrets.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-FOR-006 - PCAP payload obfuscation
objects.description: Flag is split across packets, tunnelled in odd fields (ICMP data, DNS labels), or encoded before transmission. | ATT&CK complementarity: Complements C2/exfil tactics conceptually but the CTFT entry is about packet-level reassembly and decoding.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-FOR-006 - Reassemble and decode hidden network payloads
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Follow streams, filter by protocol, export objects, then decode the reassembled payload. || FORENSIC (analyst): Reconstruct sessions and extract transferred objects; covert channels show up as anomalous field usage or unusual protocol volume.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-STE-001 - LSB image steganography
objects.description: Bits of the secret are written into the least-significant bits of pixel channels, leaving the image visually unchanged. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent; pure steganalysis.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-STE-001 - Extract least-significant-bit payloads
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Run LSB extractors across channels/bit-planes; visual bit-plane inspection reveals embedded structure. || FORENSIC (analyst): Bit-plane and chi-square analysis flags non-natural LSB distributions characteristic of embedding.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-STE-002 - Appended data / polyglot after EOF
objects.description: A second file (zip, flag.txt) is concatenated after a valid image's end-of-image marker, so viewers ignore it. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-STE-002 - Detect and split appended/embedded files
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Scan for embedded signatures and carve the trailing file; unzip/extract it. || FORENSIC (analyst): Entropy + signature scanning reveals additional file structures beyond the declared container length.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-STE-003 - Audio spectrogram hiding
objects.description: Text or a QR is drawn into frequency content so it is inaudible but visible in a spectrogram. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-STE-003 - Reveal data in the audio spectrogram
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Open the file in a spectrogram view and adjust window/contrast to read the embedded content. || FORENSIC (analyst): Spectral analysis exposes synthetic frequency artifacts that natural audio would not contain.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-STE-004 - Metadata / EXIF embedding
objects.description: The secret sits in EXIF/XMP/ID3 comment, GPS or maker-note fields rather than the visible content. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-STE-004 - Extract concealed metadata fields
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Dump all metadata and inspect comment/user fields and GPS tags. || FORENSIC (analyst): Full metadata extraction surfaces author-injected fields and inconsistencies versus the file's apparent origin.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-STE-005 - Zero-width / whitespace text steganography
objects.description: Zero-width or whitespace characters encode bits inside otherwise normal text. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-STE-005 - Decode invisible-character payloads
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Normalize/inspect code points and map zero-width sequences back to bits/characters. || FORENSIC (analyst): Unicode code-point inspection reveals non-printing characters that should not appear in plain prose.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-CRY-001 - Weak RSA parameter design
objects.description: The author ships RSA with an exploitable weakness: tiny e, close primes, shared modulus, or partial key leakage. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent; applied cryptanalysis.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-CRY-001 - Recover the RSA private key from weak parameters
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Identify the weakness class and apply the matching attack (Fermat, Wiener, common-modulus, Coppersmith). || FORENSIC (analyst): Documenting the parameter weakness explains how plaintext was recoverable without the key custodian.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-CRY-002 - Classical cipher layering
objects.description: The flag is wrapped in stacked classical ciphers (ROT/Caesar, Vigenere, substitution) to resist a single pass. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-CRY-002 - Break layered classical ciphers
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Use frequency analysis and automated solvers, peeling one layer at a time. || FORENSIC (analyst): Statistical language analysis identifies cipher families and confirms successful decryption.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-CRY-003 - Repeating-key XOR / ECB pattern
objects.description: Data is XORed with a short repeating key, or encrypted in ECB so identical blocks leak structure. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-CRY-003 - Exploit key reuse and block-mode patterns
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Recover XOR key length via Hamming distance then solve per byte; for ECB, use block cut-and-paste. || FORENSIC (analyst): Repeated ciphertext blocks are a tell-tale of ECB and of structural leakage in the design.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-CRY-004 - Predictable PRNG / nonce reuse
objects.description: A weak/seeded PRNG (LCG, time-seeded) or a reused ECDSA/CTR nonce undermines the scheme. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-CRY-004 - Reconstruct keys from broken randomness
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Recover PRNG state from outputs, or recover the ECDSA private key from two signatures sharing a nonce. || FORENSIC (analyst): Nonce reuse and predictable seeds are documented as the root cause enabling key recovery.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-CRY-005 - Hash length-extension exposure
objects.description: A MAC built as H(secret || message) with a Merkle-Damgard hash lets an attacker append data. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-CRY-005 - Forge data via length extension
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Use a length-extension tool with the known digest and length to forge a valid extended message. || FORENSIC (analyst): The vulnerability report attributes forgery to the insecure secret-prefix MAC construction.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-CRY-006 - Nested encoding obfuscation
objects.description: The flag is buried under stacked encodings (base64/base85/base32/hex/url) to look like ciphertext. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-CRY-006 - Unwrap chained encodings
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Detect each encoding by alphabet/padding and decode iteratively until plaintext appears. || FORENSIC (analyst): An encoding chain is recoverable without a key and is distinguished from genuine encryption.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-REV-001 - Anti-debugging / anti-analysis guards
objects.description: The binary detects debuggers/VMs/timing and alters behaviour or refuses to reveal the flag logic. | ATT&CK complementarity: Complements T1622/T1497 (debugger/sandbox evasion); CTFT adds the reach-the-check workflow.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-REV-001 - Bypass anti-analysis to reach the check
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Identify and patch or hook the detection routines, then debug to the comparison. || FORENSIC (analyst): Mapping the guards documents the binary's evasive intent and how analysis was restored.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-REV-002 - Packing / runtime self-modification
objects.description: Code is packed (UPX/custom) or decrypts itself at runtime so static strings/logic are hidden. | ATT&CK complementarity: Complements T1027.002 (Software Packing) with CTF unpack-and-dump procedure.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-REV-002 - Unpack and dump the real code
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Run to the original entry point and dump the unpacked image, or statically reverse the stub. || FORENSIC (analyst): Memory dumping recovers the true payload that on-disk static analysis could not see.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-REV-003 - Control-flow obfuscation / opaque predicates
objects.description: Flattening, junk branches and opaque predicates make the real path hard to follow. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-REV-003 - Deobfuscate flattened control flow
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Use symbolic/concolic execution to find the path that satisfies the flag check. || FORENSIC (analyst): Recovering the real CFG documents the obfuscation scheme and the intended logic.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-REV-004 - Custom VM / bytecode interpreter
objects.description: The flag check runs on a bespoke virtual machine whose opcodes must be understood first. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-REV-004 - Reconstruct the VM and lift its bytecode
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Reverse the dispatch loop to recover opcode semantics, then disassemble/lift the bytecode. || FORENSIC (analyst): A documented opcode table turns an opaque interpreter into reviewable logic.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-REV-005 - Constraint-gated flag check
objects.description: The binary validates input against arithmetic/bitwise constraints rather than comparing to a stored flag. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-REV-005 - Solve the check with an SMT/symbolic engine
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Model the constraints and solve for the satisfying input that is the flag. || FORENSIC (analyst): Extracting the constraint set proves how the flag was derived rather than stored.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-PWN-001 - Hidden win-function backdoor
objects.description: An unreferenced function prints the flag/spawns a shell, gated behind a vulnerable input. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent; exploitation mechanics, not adversary behaviour.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-PWN-001 - Redirect execution to the win function
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Overflow saved control data and redirect execution (ret2win), defeating any leak/canary first. || FORENSIC (analyst): The exploit path documents the missing bounds check enabling control-flow hijack.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-PWN-002 - Format-string information hiding
objects.description: A user-controlled format string both leaks memory (secrets/canary) and enables targeted writes. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-PWN-002 - Leak and overwrite via format string
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Use %p/%s to leak, then %n-style writes to redirect execution or overwrite the GOT. || FORENSIC (analyst): The vulnerability report attributes the leak/overwrite to unsanitized format arguments.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-PWN-003 - Heap-grooming puzzle
objects.description: The flag/control is reachable only by manipulating allocator metadata (use-after-free, tcache). | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-PWN-003 - Groom the heap to corrupt allocator metadata
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Shape allocations to trigger overlapping chunks or arbitrary write, then hijack a pointer. || FORENSIC (analyst): Documenting the allocation sequence explains the metadata corruption primitive.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-PWN-004 - Stripped/static gadget search

objects.name: CTFTCTE-PWN-004 - Build a ROP chain from available gadgets
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Enumerate gadgets and assemble a ROP chain to call execve or print the flag. || FORENSIC (analyst): The chain shows how existing code was repurposed despite NX/no convenient symbols.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-PWN-005 - seccomp-restricted shell puzzle
objects.description: execve is filtered, so a shell is impossible; only file I/O syscalls remain. | ATT&CK complementarity: No ATT&CK equivalent.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-PWN-005 - Open-Read-Write the flag under seccomp
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Build an ORW chain (open, read, write) via ROP/shellcode to read the flag file directly. || FORENSIC (analyst): Reading the seccomp policy reveals the allowed syscall surface that the solve relied on.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-WEB-001 - Obscured endpoint / source-comment hiding
objects.description: The flag route is unlinked, hinted in comments, robots.txt, JS bundles or backup files. | ATT&CK complementarity: Complements T1083/T1595 (discovery/recon) but is CTF content-discovery craft.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-WEB-001 - Content discovery and source review
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Brute force paths/parameters and review client source/maps for hidden references. || FORENSIC (analyst): Access logs of the discovery sweep document how the hidden surface was found.
Counter-technique recovers/defeats the paired design technique.

objects.name: CTFTTE-WEB-002 - IDOR / predictable object obscurity
objects.description: The flag belongs to another object/user reachable by guessing an ID the UI never exposes. | ATT&CK complementarity: No direct ATT&CK technique; web authorization-flaw craft.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-WEB-002 - Enumerate insecure direct object references
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Iterate identifiers/parameters to access objects outside the intended scope. || FORENSIC (analyst): Sequential access to non-owned IDs in logs is the signature of IDOR abuse.

objects.name: CTFTTE-WEB-003 - JWT misconfiguration

objects.name: CTFTCTE-WEB-003 - Forge or downgrade a JSON Web Token
objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Strip/replace the algorithm, crack the secret, or perform RS256->HS256 confusion to forge a token. || FORENSIC (analyst): Token validation logs reveal accepted tokens with unexpected alg/signature.

objects.name: CTFTCTE-WEB-004 - Extract data via blind injection

objects.name: CTFTCTE-WEB-005 - Exploit template evaluation

objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Decompile to Java/smali and grep resources/strings for the secret. || FORENSIC (analyst): Static review of the package documents secrets shipped inside the artifact.

objects.description: OFFENSIVE (solver): Decompile and rename systematically, decrypting strings to locate the logic. || FORENSIC (analyst): A reconstructed call graph documents the obfuscation and the recovered routine.
